# Cuts the GitHub release automatically when a version bump lands on main:
# CI green on a main commit whose pyproject version has no tag yet → create
# release v<version> (tag + notes from the bump PR) → dispatch the container

on:
    branches: [main]
  pull-requests: read # bump-PR title/body for the release notes
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
      - name: Detect untagged version bump
        id: version
          version=$(grep -Pom1 '^version = "\K[^"]+' pyproject.toml)
          echo "version=$version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          if gh api "repos/${{ github.repository }}/git/ref/tags/v$version" --silent 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "v$version already tagged — nothing to cut."
        if: steps.version.outputs.cut == 'true'
          VERSION: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
          # Title theme from the bump PR (the human-curated one-liner); the
          gh release create "v$VERSION" \
            --title "v$VERSION — $theme"
        if: steps.version.outputs.cut == 'true'
          VERSION: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
          # GITHUB_TOKEN-created tags don't fire `on: push: tags` — dispatch
          gh workflow run "Container Build & Publish" --ref "v$VERSION"

name: Release Cut

# Cuts the GitHub release automatically when a version bump lands on main:
# CI green on a main commit whose pyproject version has no tag yet → create
# release v<version> (tag + notes from the bump PR) → dispatch the container
# build on the new tag.
#
# Two invariants this workflow exists to keep (RELEASE.md §5):
# - The release must exist BEFORE the tag's container build finishes, because
#   that build uploads web-dist.tar.gz onto it. Creating the release first and
#   only then dispatching the build makes the ordering structural.
# - Tags created with GITHUB_TOKEN do not trigger `on: push: tags` workflows
#   (GitHub anti-recursion), so the container build is dispatched explicitly
#   via workflow_dispatch on the tag ref.
#
# The version BUMP stays a human decision in the PR; only the cut is
# mechanized. No-ops: non-bump merges (tag already exists) and CI failures.
# Never deletes or force-moves a tag; re-runs are idempotent.

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [CI]
    types: [completed]
    branches: [main]

concurrency:
  group: release-cut
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write # create the tag + release
  actions: write # dispatch container-build on the tag
  pull-requests: read # bump-PR title/body for the release notes

jobs:
  cut:
    if: github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
          fetch-depth: 1

      - name: Detect untagged version bump
        id: version
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          version=$(grep -Pom1 '^version = "\K[^"]+' pyproject.toml)
          echo "version=$version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          if gh api "repos/${{ github.repository }}/git/ref/tags/v$version" --silent 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "v$version already tagged — nothing to cut."
            echo "cut=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "cut=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

      - name: Create release
        if: steps.version.outputs.cut == 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          VERSION: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
        run: |
          # Title theme from the bump PR (the human-curated one-liner); the
          # body is GitHub's generated notes — both editable after the fact.
          theme=$(gh api "repos/${{ github.repository }}/commits/$HEAD_SHA/pulls" \
            --jq '.[0].title // empty' || true)
          theme=${theme:-release}
          gh release create "v$VERSION" \
            --target "$HEAD_SHA" \
            --generate-notes \
            --title "v$VERSION — $theme"

      - name: Dispatch container build on the tag
        if: steps.version.outputs.cut == 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          VERSION: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
        run: |
          # GITHUB_TOKEN-created tags don't fire `on: push: tags` — dispatch
          # the build explicitly on the tag ref (same github.ref semantics).
          gh workflow run "Container Build & Publish" --ref "v$VERSION"

1	# Release & Contribution Runbook
2	
3	How we branch, commit, PR, version, and tag in this repo. Read this before opening
4	a PR or cutting a release. The conventions below are what CI and the build
5	pipeline actually enforce — follow them and merges/builds stay green.
6	
7	The forge is **GitHub** (`git@github.com:nrmeyers/agentalloy.git`). Use the `gh`
8	CLI for PRs, merges, and checks.
9	
10	---
11	
12	## 1. Branching
13	
14	- Never commit feature/fix work directly to `main`. Branch first.
15	- Branch name: `type/short-kebab-summary`, where `type` matches the commit type —
16	  e.g. `fix/orientation-delivery-and-build-gate`, `feat/tier1-instruction-viewer`.
17	- Keep one logical change per branch. Don't bundle unrelated work-in-progress; if
18	  the working tree has unrelated changes, `git stash` them before branching.
19	
20	**Everything goes through a PR.** `main` has branch protection with required
21	status checks (since v6.0.0), so direct pushes to `main` are rejected — even
22	docs-only chores need a branch + PR.
23	
24	**Stacked PRs** (a PR based on another feature branch) get CI from birth — the
25	`pull_request` trigger has no branch filter. But squash-merging still breaks
26	naive stacking: see the gotcha in §7 for the retarget/rebase recipe.
27	
28	## 2. Commits
29	
30	Conventional Commits with a scope: `type(scope): subject`.
31	
32	- Types in use: `feat`, `fix`, `chore`, `docs`, `ci`, `perf`, `style`, `test`.
33	- Subject in imperative mood, lower-case, no trailing period.
34	- Body explains the *why* and the root cause, not just the *what*.
35	- End every commit with the trailer (use the actual authoring model's name):
36	
37	  ```
38	  Co-Authored-By: Claude <model> <noreply@anthropic.com>
39	  ```
40	
41	## 3. Pull requests
42	
43	1. Push the branch: `git push -u origin <branch>`.
44	2. Open the PR against `main` with `gh pr create --base main`.
45	3. PR title = the same Conventional-Commit summary; append the target version when
46	   the PR carries a release, e.g. `... (v3.5.2)`.
47	4. PR body: Context → the problem/root cause → the fix → tests. End with:
48	
49	   ```
50	   🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
51	   ```
52	
53	5. Arm auto-merge (repo has it enabled; branches auto-delete on merge):
54	
55	   ```
56	   gh pr merge <N> --auto --squash
57	   ```
58	
59	   The merge fires when the required checks go green. Squash-merge is the
60	   convention — each commit on `main` reads `type(scope): subject (#N)`.
61	   Merging into `main` is gated; get explicit authorization first.
62	
63	### CI gates (required checks, enforced by branch protection)
64	
65	Four required checks on `main`: **`quality`**, **`container-tests`**,
66	**`pipx-smoke`**, **`web-build`** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`). A PR cannot
67	merge red.
68	
69	- `quality`: `uv sync --frozen --extra code-index` → ruff check → ruff format
70	  --check (formatting is checked **separately** from lint; run `uv run ruff
71	  format` before pushing) → pyright → `pytest -m "not integration and not
72	  container"` → pack version-bump guard.
73	- `container-tests`: builds the deploy image with real podman and runs the
74	  `container`-marked tests. Runs in parallel with `quality`; skips itself
75	  (still reporting green) when the diff is docs/images only.
76	- `pipx-smoke`: builds the core wheel, installs it isolated, smoke-tests the
77	  CLI surface (including that the `[code-index]` extra is genuinely optional).
78	- `web-build`: the same tsc + vite build the release pipeline uses.
79	
80	Reproduce locally before pushing:
81	
82	```
83	uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check . && uv run pyright \
84	  && uv run pytest -m "not integration and not container"
85	```
86	
87	The `-m integration` suite (needs a live embed server on 47951) never runs on
88	PRs — it runs nightly (`corpus-nightly.yml`, `integration-tests` job); failures
89	open an issue labeled `nightly-integration`. Run it locally before risky
90	retrieval/embedding changes: `uv run pytest -m integration`.
91	
92	Tests live under `tests/` and cover the install pipeline (`tests/install/`),
93	retrieval, composition, applicability filtering, telemetry, and the
94	harness-wiring catalog.
95	
96	## 4. Versioning (SemVer)
97	
98	Version lives in `pyproject.toml` (`[project] version`). Bump per
99	[SemVer](https://semver.org/), where every tier refers to **shipped code
100	only**: **patch** = bug fix to shipped behavior, **minor** =
101	backward-compatible feature, **major** = breaking change. Changes outside the
102	shipped surface (CI, docs, tests, tooling) have no SemVer tier — they don't
103	version at all (see below).
104	
105	### When a bump is required: shipped-surface lockstep
106	
107	The invariant is NOT "main == last tag" — it is **"a tag's version tells the
108	truth about shipped content"**: two tags with different versions always differ
109	in what users actually run. Mechanically:
110	
111	- A merge **requires a version bump** when its diff touches the **shipped
112	  surface**: `src/`, `src/agentalloy/_packs/`, `frontend/`, `Containerfile*` /
113	  `container/`, or dependency pins in `pyproject.toml` / `uv.lock`.
114	- The bump **rides the shipped-surface PR itself** — do not open a separate
115	  `chore(release)` bump PR; merging the bumped PR IS cutting the release
116	  (§5). When several shipped PRs deliberately accumulate before a release,
117	  the final PR of the batch carries the bump.
118	- Merges touching only CI workflows, docs, tests, or repo tooling do **not**
119	  bump. Main being ahead of the last tag by that class of change is not
120	  drift — it's the definition.
121	- Never cut a release tag while unversioned shipped-surface changes sit on
122	  `main`; bump first.
123	
124	Rationale: upgrades are not free for users (multi-GB container pull, upgrade
125	paths with real failure modes), and the release-check nudges every install.
126	Don't spend that on housekeeping — release when shipped value has accumulated.
127	The test for "internal change" is just: *does the wheel or image change?* —
128	answerable from the diff paths. (v6.1.1 predates this rule: it shipped a
129	byte-identical wheel for CI-only changes; harmless, but the nudge was wasted.)
130	
131	When you bump the version you MUST also:
132	
133	- **Regenerate and commit `uv.lock`** in the same change — the lock pins
134	  `agentalloy`'s own version, so a `pyproject`-only bump leaves them drifted. CI
135	  uses `uv sync --frozen` (uses the lock as-is) and will **not** catch the drift;
136	  it only bites a `uv sync --locked` run or a merge. Verify with `uv lock --check`
137	  (output `Resolved N packages` = clean).
138	
139	- **Bump the touched pack's `version`** if you edited any `src/agentalloy/_packs/<pack>/`
140	  content (e.g. `pack.yaml`). Pack propagation is version-gated by design (preserves
141	  the SkillVersion rollback chain), and a CI guard fails the PR on a content edit
142	  without a version bump.
143	
144	## 5. Cutting a release
145	
146	The cut is **automated**: when a PR carrying a version bump (a shipped-surface
147	PR with the bump riding along, per §4) merges to main and that commit's CI
148	goes green, `Release Cut` (`.github/workflows/release-cut.yml`) creates the
149	GitHub release `v<X.Y.Z>` (tag on the merge commit, title themed from the
150	bumping PR, generated notes) and dispatches `Container Build & Publish` on
151	the new tag. Merging the bumped PR IS cutting the release — nothing to run.
152	
153	What the automation guarantees, and why it's shaped this way:
154	
155	- The **release exists before the tag build finishes** — `container-build.yml`
156	  uploads `web-dist.tar.gz` onto it with `gh release upload`, so the release
157	  is created first and the build dispatched second.
158	- The tag build publishes the release-pinned
159	  `ghcr.io/nrmeyers/agentalloy:v<X.Y.Z>` image (corpus baked in) and attaches
160	  the version-matched `web-dist.tar.gz` to the release.
161	- The build is **dispatched explicitly** (`workflow_dispatch --ref v<X.Y.Z>`)
162	  because tags created with `GITHUB_TOKEN` do not fire `on: push: tags`
163	  workflows.
164	- Non-bump merges and re-runs are no-ops (version already tagged); a red CI
165	  run cuts nothing. The version bump itself stays a human decision in the PR
166	  (§4) — only the cut is mechanized.
167	- Release title/notes are editable after the fact (`gh release edit`); the
168	  automation never touches an existing release or tag.
169	
170	Confirm completion with `gh run list --workflow container-build.yml` and
171	check the asset landed: `gh release view v<X.Y.Z> --json assets`.
172	
173	**Manual fallback** (automation down or cutting from an unusual state):
174	
175	```
176	git checkout main && git pull --ff-only origin main
177	gh release create v<X.Y.Z> --target main --generate-notes \
178	  --title "v<X.Y.Z> — <one-line theme>"
179	```
180	
181	The tag must point at the squash-merge commit on `main` (where `pyproject`
182	already reads the new version) — never a feature-branch commit. A manually
183	pushed tag (your credentials, not `GITHUB_TOKEN`) triggers the container
184	build itself; don't also dispatch it.
185	
186	## 6. Quick checklist
187	
188	- [ ] Branch off `main`, one logical change.
189	- [ ] Conventional-Commit messages + `Co-Authored-By` trailer.
190	- [ ] Version bumped in `pyproject.toml` (if releasing); `uv.lock` regenerated
191	      (`uv lock --check` clean); touched pack `version` bumped.
192	- [ ] Local gate green: ruff check + ruff format --check + pyright + pytest.
193	- [ ] PR opened against `main`, required checks green, squash-merged with
194	      authorization (`gh pr merge --auto --squash`).
195	- [ ] If the PR bumped the version: `Release Cut` created `v<X.Y.Z>` after CI
196	      went green; container build + web-dist asset confirmed.
197	
198	## 7. Gotchas seen in past releases
199	
200	These have bitten releases before; surface them up-front when planning a tag.
201	
202	- **Merging a squash-based stacked-PR train.** Each PR targets its
203	  predecessor's branch; after the predecessor squash-merges, retarget the next
204	  PR at `main` — GitHub does NOT retarget for you here. A plain `git rebase
205	  main` usually works (patch-id detection skips already-squashed commits), but
206	  it CONFLICTS when the predecessor's squash contained extra commits touching
207	  the same files (patch-ids no longer match). Recipe that always works: replay
208	  only the branch's own commits — `git rebase --onto origin/main
209	  <old-parent-sha> <branch>` — then force-push (`--force-with-lease`),
210	  `gh pr edit <N> --base main`, wait for green, merge. Repeat down the stack.
211	  (Observed on the v6.0.0 train: PRs #332/#333 conflicted after #331's squash
212	  included two fix commits; `--onto` resolved it cleanly.)
213	- **Working on a worktree branch that was already merged.** When you stack new
214	  work on a branch whose previous head already got squash-merged into `main`,
215	  GitHub sees the still-unsquashed commit as "ahead of main" and the merge ref
216	  conflicts. CI then never runs on a `pull_request` event. Fix: merge `origin/main`
217	  into the branch (resolving the trivial `pyproject.toml` / `uv.lock` conflict by
218	  taking the new-release side) and push — CI registers on the next event. Or
219	  branch fresh off `main` for the new work instead of extending the merged branch.
220	- **`gh pr merge --delete-branch` fails from a non-primary worktree.** `gh` tries
221	  to check out `main` locally to delete the merged branch, which fails when the
222	  primary worktree already has `main` checked out (`fatal: 'main' is already used
223	  by worktree at …`). The remote merge still happened — verify with
224	  `gh pr view <N> --json state,mergeCommit`. Delete the branch on the remote
225	  manually: `git push origin --delete <branch>`. (Since v6.0.0 the repo has
226	  delete-branch-on-merge enabled, so `--delete-branch` is usually unnecessary —
227	  this gotcha only applies to branches kept alive deliberately, e.g. a stack.)
228	- **Container build is the long pole.** `Container Build & Publish`'s `build-corpus`
229	  job re-ingests + re-embeds every pack into the image; with new packs or
230	  resliced fragments this can run ~55 min (observed on v5.1.0, which added one
231	  pack skill; vs ~6 min for a code-only release). The workflow tolerates up to
232	  150 min — don't panic at 45-min marks. The
233	  `main`-push build and the tag-push build run concurrently and don't share the

# Release & Contribution Runbook

How we branch, commit, PR, version, and tag in this repo. Read this before opening
a PR or cutting a release. The conventions below are what CI and the build
pipeline actually enforce — follow them and merges/builds stay green.

The forge is **GitHub** (`git@github.com:nrmeyers/agentalloy.git`). Use the `gh`
CLI for PRs, merges, and checks.

---

## 1. Branching

- Never commit feature/fix work directly to `main`. Branch first.
- Branch name: `type/short-kebab-summary`, where `type` matches the commit type —
  e.g. `fix/orientation-delivery-and-build-gate`, `feat/tier1-instruction-viewer`.
- Keep one logical change per branch. Don't bundle unrelated work-in-progress; if
  the working tree has unrelated changes, `git stash` them before branching.

**Everything goes through a PR.** `main` has branch protection with required
status checks (since v6.0.0), so direct pushes to `main` are rejected — even
docs-only chores need a branch + PR.

**Stacked PRs** (a PR based on another feature branch) get CI from birth — the
`pull_request` trigger has no branch filter. But squash-merging still breaks
naive stacking: see the gotcha in §7 for the retarget/rebase recipe.

## 2. Commits

Conventional Commits with a scope: `type(scope): subject`.

- Types in use: `feat`, `fix`, `chore`, `docs`, `ci`, `perf`, `style`, `test`.
- Subject in imperative mood, lower-case, no trailing period.
- Body explains the *why* and the root cause, not just the *what*.
- End every commit with the trailer (use the actual authoring model's name):

  ```
  Co-Authored-By: Claude <model> <noreply@anthropic.com>
  ```

## 3. Pull requests

1. Push the branch: `git push -u origin <branch>`.
2. Open the PR against `main` with `gh pr create --base main`.
3. PR title = the same Conventional-Commit summary; append the target version when
   the PR carries a release, e.g. `... (v3.5.2)`.
4. PR body: Context → the problem/root cause → the fix → tests. End with:

   ```
   🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
   ```

5. Arm auto-merge (repo has it enabled; branches auto-delete on merge):

   ```
   gh pr merge <N> --auto --squash
   ```

   The merge fires when the required checks go green. Squash-merge is the
   convention — each commit on `main` reads `type(scope): subject (#N)`.
   Merging into `main` is gated; get explicit authorization first.

### CI gates (required checks, enforced by branch protection)

Four required checks on `main`: **`quality`**, **`container-tests`**,
**`pipx-smoke`**, **`web-build`** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`). A PR cannot
merge red.

- `quality`: `uv sync --frozen --extra code-index` → ruff check → ruff format
  --check (formatting is checked **separately** from lint; run `uv run ruff
  format` before pushing) → pyright → `pytest -m "not integration and not
  container"` → pack version-bump guard.
- `container-tests`: builds the deploy image with real podman and runs the
  `container`-marked tests. Runs in parallel with `quality`; skips itself
  (still reporting green) when the diff is docs/images only.
- `pipx-smoke`: builds the core wheel, installs it isolated, smoke-tests the
  CLI surface (including that the `[code-index]` extra is genuinely optional).
- `web-build`: the same tsc + vite build the release pipeline uses.

Reproduce locally before pushing:

```
uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check . && uv run pyright \
  && uv run pytest -m "not integration and not container"
```

The `-m integration` suite (needs a live embed server on 47951) never runs on
PRs — it runs nightly (`corpus-nightly.yml`, `integration-tests` job); failures
open an issue labeled `nightly-integration`. Run it locally before risky
retrieval/embedding changes: `uv run pytest -m integration`.

Tests live under `tests/` and cover the install pipeline (`tests/install/`),
retrieval, composition, applicability filtering, telemetry, and the
harness-wiring catalog.

## 4. Versioning (SemVer)

Version lives in `pyproject.toml` (`[project] version`). Bump per
[SemVer](https://semver.org/), where every tier refers to **shipped code
only**: **patch** = bug fix to shipped behavior, **minor** =
backward-compatible feature, **major** = breaking change. Changes outside the
shipped surface (CI, docs, tests, tooling) have no SemVer tier — they don't
version at all (see below).

### When a bump is required: shipped-surface lockstep

The invariant is NOT "main == last tag" — it is **"a tag's version tells the
truth about shipped content"**: two tags with different versions always differ
in what users actually run. Mechanically:

- A merge **requires a version bump** when its diff touches the **shipped
  surface**: `src/`, `src/agentalloy/_packs/`, `frontend/`, `Containerfile*` /
  `container/`, or dependency pins in `pyproject.toml` / `uv.lock`.
- The bump **rides the shipped-surface PR itself** — do not open a separate
  `chore(release)` bump PR; merging the bumped PR IS cutting the release
  (§5). When several shipped PRs deliberately accumulate before a release,
  the final PR of the batch carries the bump.
- Merges touching only CI workflows, docs, tests, or repo tooling do **not**
  bump. Main being ahead of the last tag by that class of change is not
  drift — it's the definition.
- Never cut a release tag while unversioned shipped-surface changes sit on
  `main`; bump first.

Rationale: upgrades are not free for users (multi-GB container pull, upgrade
paths with real failure modes), and the release-check nudges every install.
Don't spend that on housekeeping — release when shipped value has accumulated.
The test for "internal change" is just: *does the wheel or image change?* —
answerable from the diff paths. (v6.1.1 predates this rule: it shipped a
byte-identical wheel for CI-only changes; harmless, but the nudge was wasted.)

When you bump the version you MUST also:

- **Regenerate and commit `uv.lock`** in the same change — the lock pins
  `agentalloy`'s own version, so a `pyproject`-only bump leaves them drifted. CI
  uses `uv sync --frozen` (uses the lock as-is) and will **not** catch the drift;
  it only bites a `uv sync --locked` run or a merge. Verify with `uv lock --check`
  (output `Resolved N packages` = clean).

- **Bump the touched pack's `version`** if you edited any `src/agentalloy/_packs/<pack>/`
  content (e.g. `pack.yaml`). Pack propagation is version-gated by design (preserves
  the SkillVersion rollback chain), and a CI guard fails the PR on a content edit
  without a version bump.

## 5. Cutting a release

The cut is **automated**: when a PR carrying a version bump (a shipped-surface
PR with the bump riding along, per §4) merges to main and that commit's CI
goes green, `Release Cut` (`.github/workflows/release-cut.yml`) creates the
GitHub release `v<X.Y.Z>` (tag on the merge commit, title themed from the
bumping PR, generated notes) and dispatches `Container Build & Publish` on
the new tag. Merging the bumped PR IS cutting the release — nothing to run.

What the automation guarantees, and why it's shaped this way:

- The **release exists before the tag build finishes** — `container-build.yml`
  uploads `web-dist.tar.gz` onto it with `gh release upload`, so the release
  is created first and the build dispatched second.
- The tag build publishes the release-pinned
  `ghcr.io/nrmeyers/agentalloy:v<X.Y.Z>` image (corpus baked in) and attaches
  the version-matched `web-dist.tar.gz` to the release.
- The build is **dispatched explicitly** (`workflow_dispatch --ref v<X.Y.Z>`)
  because tags created with `GITHUB_TOKEN` do not fire `on: push: tags`
  workflows.
- Non-bump merges and re-runs are no-ops (version already tagged); a red CI
  run cuts nothing. The version bump itself stays a human decision in the PR
  (§4) — only the cut is mechanized.
- Release title/notes are editable after the fact (`gh release edit`); the
  automation never touches an existing release or tag.

Confirm completion with `gh run list --workflow container-build.yml` and
check the asset landed: `gh release view v<X.Y.Z> --json assets`.

**Manual fallback** (automation down or cutting from an unusual state):

```
git checkout main && git pull --ff-only origin main
gh release create v<X.Y.Z> --target main --generate-notes \
  --title "v<X.Y.Z> — <one-line theme>"
```

The tag must point at the squash-merge commit on `main` (where `pyproject`
already reads the new version) — never a feature-branch commit. A manually
pushed tag (your credentials, not `GITHUB_TOKEN`) triggers the container
build itself; don't also dispatch it.

## 6. Quick checklist

- [ ] Branch off `main`, one logical change.
- [ ] Conventional-Commit messages + `Co-Authored-By` trailer.
- [ ] Version bumped in `pyproject.toml` (if releasing); `uv.lock` regenerated
      (`uv lock --check` clean); touched pack `version` bumped.
- [ ] Local gate green: ruff check + ruff format --check + pyright + pytest.
- [ ] PR opened against `main`, required checks green, squash-merged with
      authorization (`gh pr merge --auto --squash`).
- [ ] If the PR bumped the version: `Release Cut` created `v<X.Y.Z>` after CI
      went green; container build + web-dist asset confirmed.

## 7. Gotchas seen in past releases

These have bitten releases before; surface them up-front when planning a tag.

- **Merging a squash-based stacked-PR train.** Each PR targets its
  predecessor's branch; after the predecessor squash-merges, retarget the next
  PR at `main` — GitHub does NOT retarget for you here. A plain `git rebase
  main` usually works (patch-id detection skips already-squashed commits), but
  it CONFLICTS when the predecessor's squash contained extra commits touching
  the same files (patch-ids no longer match). Recipe that always works: replay
  only the branch's own commits — `git rebase --onto origin/main
  <old-parent-sha> <branch>` — then force-push (`--force-with-lease`),
  `gh pr edit <N> --base main`, wait for green, merge. Repeat down the stack.
  (Observed on the v6.0.0 train: PRs #332/#333 conflicted after #331's squash
  included two fix commits; `--onto` resolved it cleanly.)
- **Working on a worktree branch that was already merged.** When you stack new
  work on a branch whose previous head already got squash-merged into `main`,
  GitHub sees the still-unsquashed commit as "ahead of main" and the merge ref
  conflicts. CI then never runs on a `pull_request` event. Fix: merge `origin/main`
  into the branch (resolving the trivial `pyproject.toml` / `uv.lock` conflict by
  taking the new-release side) and push — CI registers on the next event. Or
  branch fresh off `main` for the new work instead of extending the merged branch.
- **`gh pr merge --delete-branch` fails from a non-primary worktree.** `gh` tries
  to check out `main` locally to delete the merged branch, which fails when the
  primary worktree already has `main` checked out (`fatal: 'main' is already used
  by worktree at …`). The remote merge still happened — verify with
  `gh pr view <N> --json state,mergeCommit`. Delete the branch on the remote
  manually: `git push origin --delete <branch>`. (Since v6.0.0 the repo has
  delete-branch-on-merge enabled, so `--delete-branch` is usually unnecessary —
  this gotcha only applies to branches kept alive deliberately, e.g. a stack.)
- **Container build is the long pole.** `Container Build & Publish`'s `build-corpus`
  job re-ingests + re-embeds every pack into the image; with new packs or
  resliced fragments this can run ~55 min (observed on v5.1.0, which added one
  pack skill; vs ~6 min for a code-only release). The workflow tolerates up to
  150 min — don't panic at 45-min marks. The
  `main`-push build and the tag-push build run concurrently and don't share the
  embed cache, so total wall time roughly doubles for big releases. Users get the
  new code via `:latest` from the `main`-push as soon as that finishes; the
  `:vX.Y.Z` pinned image follows when the tag build completes.
- **`enable-service` silently skips the rerank/embed units when `llama-server`
  isn't on PATH.** `shutil.which("llama-server")` returns `None` if the
  `pull-models`-generated `~/.local/bin/llama-server` shim was deleted (e.g. by
  `uv tool install --reinstall`). The fallout: rerank/embed services aren't
  registered, no warmup, Stage B disabled. Verify the shim exists before running
  `enable-service`, and recreate it via `agentalloy pull-models` if missing.

## The fix: derive the bump automatically from the PR's Conventional-Commit type

- Reads the **PR title** (`feat!`/`BREAKING`→major, `feat`→minor, `fix`/`perf`→patch; `docs/ci/test/chore/style`→none) for the **tier**.
- Gates **whether** to bump on the existing §4 shipped-surface path rule (`src/`, `_packs/`, `frontend/`, container, dep pins) — so docs/CI-only PRs still don't version.
- Computes next version, edits `pyproject.toml`, runs `uv lock`, commits to the PR branch. Idempotent (no-op if already bumped vs base).
- Tier logic lives in a **tested Python module** (mirrors your `test_pack_version_bump_guard.py`), workflow just calls it.
- Becomes a **required check** so auto-merge physically can't fire on an un-bumped SHA. `release-cut.yml` stays untouched.

This works identically across every session/LLM because it's server-side in CI — no one has to know the rules.

# Plan: Fully automatic SemVer bumps from PR type

## Context

Version bumps were never truly automatic. `release-cut.yml` auto-cuts the tag +
release when an **untagged** version lands on `main`, but RELEASE.md §4/§5
deliberately keep *"the version BUMP a human decision in the PR"* — the tier
(major/minor/patch), the `pyproject.toml` edit, and the `uv.lock` regen all
depend on whoever drives that session. PRs #432/#433 folded the bump into the
fix PR (good) but still leaned on the human/LLM to pick the tier and keep the
lock synced. Result: inconsistency across sessions/LLMs and the recurring
`uv.lock` drift.

**Goal:** derive the bump tier automatically from the PR's Conventional-Commit
type and apply the `pyproject`+`uv.lock` edit in CI, so it happens identically
regardless of session or LLM. No standalone `chore(release)` commits.
`release-cut.yml` stays untouched.

## Design decisions (confirmed with user)

- **Push token:** fine-grained PAT in repo secret `BUMP_TOKEN` (Contents: write,
  Pull requests: write). Required because `GITHUB_TOKEN`-pushed commits do **not**
  trigger workflows (same anti-recursion rule `release-cut.yml:12` documents for
  tags) — the bumped SHA would get no check runs and every PR would deadlock.
  **User must create this before the first PR merges.**
- **Tier source:** PR **title** (authoritative conventional-commit string; already
  what `release-cut` reads for the theme, and what the squash subject becomes).
- **Strict merge:** enable required-branches-up-to-date on `main` to close the
  two-PRs-in-flight version-collision hole.

## Tier logic (fully deterministic — zero human judgment)

Whether-to-bump keeps the RELEASE.md §4 **shipped-surface path gate**; only the
tier is derived from type:

1. Diff touches **no** shipped surface (`src/`, `src/agentalloy/_packs/`,
   `frontend/`, `Containerfile*`/`container/`, dep pins in `pyproject.toml`/
   `uv.lock`) → **no bump** (docs/CI/test/tooling-only, per §4).
2. Else tier from PR title: `feat!` or `BREAKING CHANGE` → **major**; `feat` →
   **minor**; **everything else** (`fix`,`perf`,`refactor`,`chore`,…) → **patch**.

Rationale for "else→patch": §4's invariant is *a tag's version tells the truth
about shipped content* — any shipped-surface change must bump. Defaulting
non-feat shipped changes to patch removes the last bit of human tier judgment
while honoring §4.

## Implementation

### 1. `scripts/version_bump.py` (new) — pure logic + runnable CLI
Mirrors the pack-guard ethos (`tests/test_pack_version_bump_guard.py`): pure
functions, git I/O injected/isolated, unit-tested. Functions:
- `tier_from_title(title: str) -> Literal["major","minor","patch"] | None`
- `touches_shipped_surface(changed_files: list[str]) -> bool` (shipped globs as a
  module constant — single source of truth reused by the workflow)
- `bump(version: str, tier) -> str` (SemVer, resets lower components)
- `decide(title, changed_files, current_version) -> str | None` (composes above;
  returns next version or None)
- `__main__`: reads PR title + `git diff --name-only <base>...HEAD` + current
  `pyproject` version, prints the next version (or nothing). Idempotent: if
  current version already differs from the base version, print nothing (no-op).

### 2. `tests/test_version_bump.py` (new)
Unit-test every pure function: tier mapping incl. `feat!`/`BREAKING CHANGE`
footer, else→patch, no-shipped→none, SemVer resets (7.0.7→minor=7.1.0,
→major=8.0.0), idempotency (already-bumped base → None). Runs in the existing
`quality` job's `pytest -m "not integration and not container"` sweep.

### 3. `.github/workflows/version-bump.yml` (new)
- Trigger: `on: pull_request` (opened, synchronize, reopened, edited — `edited`
  so a title fix re-derives the tier).
- Single job `version-bump`, `runs-on: ubuntu-latest`, **always reports green**
  (required-check friendly; no-op path still exits 0).
- Steps: checkout PR **head** with `token: ${{ secrets.BUMP_TOKEN }}` and
  `fetch-depth: 0`; install uv; run `scripts/version_bump.py` against
  `${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}` and the PR title. If it emits a new
  version and the branch isn't already bumped: `sed`/write `pyproject.toml`,
  `uv lock`, `git commit` (with `Co-Authored-By` trailer per RELEASE.md §2) and
  `git push` to the PR head branch. Idempotency guard makes the re-triggered run
  (from its own push) a no-op → green → auto-merge fires on the bumped SHA.

### 4. Branch protection (via `gh api`, at execution time)
- Add `version-bump` to `required_status_checks.contexts` (so auto-merge cannot
  fire on the un-bumped SHA).
- Set `required_status_checks.strict = true` (branches up to date).
- Leaves `enforce_admins`/existing checks unchanged.

### 5. RELEASE.md §4 + §5 rewrite
Replace *"the version BUMP stays a human decision in the PR"* (§4 bullet, §5
final bullet) with the automated tier rule. Document: tier derives from PR title,
whether from shipped-surface paths, CI writes `pyproject`+`uv.lock` on the PR,
the `BUMP_TOKEN` requirement, and that a human bump on the branch is still
honored (idempotent no-op). Removes the two-policies-in-one-doc drift per the
`one-recommendation-no-residue` convention. Update §6 checklist accordingly.

## Interaction / failure-mode notes (already vetted with advisor)
- **No infinite loop:** bot push → `synchronize` re-run → idempotency guard sees
  version≠base → no-op → green.
- **Auto-merge race closed:** `version-bump` is required, so the only all-green
  SHA is the fully-bumped one.
- **Fork PRs:** N/A (solo repo); `BUMP_TOKEN` checkout assumes same-repo head.
- **Manual/LLM bump still works:** if a PR already carries a bump, the job is a
  clean no-op.
- `release-cut.yml` unchanged — it still cuts on untagged-version-on-main + green.

## Verification
1. **Unit:** `uv run pytest tests/test_version_bump.py -q` — tier/SemVer/idempotency.
2. **Full gate:** `uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check . && uv run
   pyright && uv run pytest -m "not integration and not container"`.
3. **Live end-to-end (after `BUMP_TOKEN` exists):** open a throwaway `fix:` PR
   touching a `src/` file → confirm the bump job commits `pyproject`+`uv.lock`
   to the branch, CI re-runs green on the bumped SHA, and on merge `release-cut`
   tags the derived version. Then a `docs:`-only PR → confirm **no** bump.
4. Confirm `gh api repos/nrmeyers/agentalloy/branches/main/protection` shows
   `version-bump` in contexts and `strict: true`.

## Blocker to surface at handoff
User must create the fine-grained PAT and add it as secret `BUMP_TOKEN` before
the first shipped PR merges — otherwise bump commits get no CI and PRs deadlock.

name: Version Bump

# Derives the SemVer bump automatically from the PR's Conventional-Commit title
# and writes pyproject.toml + uv.lock onto the PR branch, so the version bump is
# no longer a per-session human/LLM decision (RELEASE.md §4). Tier: feat! /
# BREAKING CHANGE → major, feat → minor, everything else touching the shipped
# surface → patch; docs/CI/test-only PRs don't bump. scripts/version_bump.py
# owns the (unit-tested) logic; this workflow is the I/O + push shell.
#
# TWO INVARIANTS this workflow depends on:
# - The bump commit MUST be pushed with a NON-default token (secret BUMP_TOKEN,
#   a fine-grained PAT with contents+PR write). GITHUB_TOKEN-pushed commits do
#   NOT trigger workflows (GitHub anti-recursion — the same rule release-cut.yml
#   documents for tags). A GITHUB_TOKEN push would leave the bumped SHA with no
#   check runs and deadlock auto-merge on the required checks.
# - This job (`version-bump`) is a REQUIRED status check. Because it only goes
#   green on the fully-bumped SHA (idempotent no-op once bumped), auto-merge can
#   never fire on the un-bumped commit.
#
# Idempotent: if the branch already carries a bump (a human/LLM did it, or this
# job's own push re-triggered the run), the script emits nothing and the job is
# a clean green no-op. release-cut.yml is untouched — it still cuts the tag when
# the untagged version lands on main and CI is green.

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, edited]

concurrency:
  group: version-bump-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read # the bump commit is pushed with BUMP_TOKEN, not GITHUB_TOKEN

jobs:
  version-bump:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Check out PR head branch
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          # head_ref = the PR's source branch (not the detached merge ref), so
          # we can commit + push back to it. fetch-depth 0: the script reads the
          # base commit's pyproject and the base..HEAD diff.
          ref: ${{ github.head_ref }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          token: ${{ secrets.BUMP_TOKEN }}

      - name: Install uv
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v3
        with:
          enable-cache: true

      - name: Compute and apply version bump
        env:
          PR_TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          next=$(uv run python scripts/version_bump.py \
            --title "$PR_TITLE" --base-sha "$BASE_SHA")

          if [ -z "$next" ]; then
            echo "No version bump warranted (no shipped-surface change, or already bumped)."
            exit 0
          fi

          echo "Deriving bump → v$next"
          # Exactly one top-level `version = "..."` line in pyproject.toml.
          sed -i -E "s/^version = \"[^\"]+\"/version = \"$next\"/" pyproject.toml
          uv lock

          git config user.name "agentalloy-release-bot"
          git config user.email "release-bot@users.noreply.github.com"
          git add pyproject.toml uv.lock
          git commit -m "chore: bump version to $next" \
            -m "Automated bump derived from the PR title's Conventional-Commit type." \
            -m "Co-Authored-By: agentalloy-release-bot <release-bot@users.noreply.github.com>"

Version lives in `pyproject.toml` (`[project] version`). Bump per
[SemVer](https://semver.org/), where every tier refers to **shipped code
only**: **patch** = bug fix to shipped behavior, **minor** =
backward-compatible feature, **major** = breaking change. Changes outside the
shipped surface (CI, docs, tests, tooling) have no SemVer tier — they don't
version at all (see below).

### When a bump is required: shipped-surface lockstep

The invariant is NOT "main == last tag" — it is **"a tag's version tells the
truth about shipped content"**: two tags with different versions always differ
in what users actually run. Mechanically:

- A merge **requires a version bump** when its diff touches the **shipped
  surface**: `src/`, `src/agentalloy/_packs/`, `frontend/`, `Containerfile*` /
  `container/`, or dependency pins in `pyproject.toml` / `uv.lock`.
- The bump **rides the shipped-surface PR itself** — do not open a separate
  `chore(release)` bump PR; merging the bumped PR IS cutting the release
  (§5). When several shipped PRs deliberately accumulate before a release,
  the final PR of the batch carries the bump.
- Merges touching only CI workflows, docs, tests, or repo tooling do **not**
  bump. Main being ahead of the last tag by that class of change is not
  drift — it's the definition.
- Never cut a release tag while unversioned shipped-surface changes sit on
  `main`; bump first.

Rationale: upgrades are not free for users (multi-GB container pull, upgrade
paths with real failure modes), and the release-check nudges every install.
Don't spend that on housekeeping — release when shipped value has accumulated.
The test for "internal change" is just: *does the wheel or image change?* —
answerable from the diff paths. (v6.1.1 predates this rule: it shipped a
byte-identical wheel for CI-only changes; harmless, but the nudge was wasted.)

  `agentalloy`'s own version, so a `pyproject`-only bump leaves them drifted. CI

  it only bites a `uv sync --locked` run or a merge. Verify with `uv lock --check`
  (output `Resolved N packages` = clean).

Version lives in `pyproject.toml` (`[project] version`). Every tier refers to
**shipped code only**: **patch** = bug fix to shipped behavior, **minor** =
backward-compatible feature, **major** = breaking change. Changes outside the
shipped surface (CI, docs, tests, tooling) have no SemVer tier — they don't
version at all.

### The bump is automatic — you do not choose the tier or edit `pyproject`

`Version Bump` (`.github/workflows/version-bump.yml`) derives and applies the
bump on every PR. You never open a `chore(release)` PR and never hand-edit the
version. Two deterministic gates (`scripts/version_bump.py`, unit-tested in
`tests/test_version_bump.py`):

- **Whether to bump — shipped-surface path gate.** A bump happens only when the
  PR's diff touches the **shipped surface**: `src/` (incl. `src/agentalloy/_packs/`),
  `frontend/`, `Containerfile*` / `container/`, or dependency pins in
  `pyproject.toml` / `uv.lock`. PRs touching only CI, docs, tests, or tooling do
  **not** bump — main being ahead of the last tag by that class of change is not
  drift, it's the definition.
- **Which tier — from the PR title's Conventional-Commit type.** `feat!` or a
  `BREAKING CHANGE` marker → **major**; `feat` → **minor**; **everything else**
  touching shipped code (`fix`, `perf`, `refactor`, `chore`, …) → **patch**. So
  the only lever you touch is the PR title — get the type right and the version
  follows.

When it fires, the workflow rewrites `pyproject.toml`, regenerates `uv.lock`,
and commits both to your PR branch (`chore: bump version to X.Y.Z`). CI re-runs
on that commit; merging the PR IS cutting the release (§5). The bump commit is
squashed away on merge, so `main` reads `type(scope): subject (#N)` as always.

The invariant this upholds: **"a tag's version tells the truth about shipped
content"** — two tags with different versions always differ in what users run.
"else → patch" honors it (any shipped-surface change versions), while `feat`
and `feat!`/`BREAKING` still escalate. Rationale for gating on shipped surface:
upgrades aren't free for users (multi-GB container pull, real upgrade failure
modes) and the release-check nudges every install — don't spend that on
housekeeping. The test for "internal change" is just: *does the wheel or image
change?*

Notes and escapes:

- **`BUMP_TOKEN` is required infra.** The bump commit is pushed with the
  fine-grained PAT in repo secret `BUMP_TOKEN` (Contents + Pull requests: write),
  not `GITHUB_TOKEN` — the default token's pushes don't trigger workflows
  (GitHub anti-recursion, same rule as tags in §5), which would leave the bumped
  commit with no checks and deadlock auto-merge. If bumps stop happening, check
  that secret first.
- **`version-bump` is a required status check.** It only goes green on the
  fully-bumped SHA, so auto-merge can't fire on an un-bumped commit.
- **A manual bump still works.** If you (or a tool) already bumped `pyproject` on
  the branch, the workflow is a clean no-op (it compares against the PR base).
- **Touched-pack version.** If you edited any `src/agentalloy/_packs/<pack>/`
  content, still bump that pack's own `version` — pack propagation is
  version-gated by design (SkillVersion rollback chain), and the `quality` job's
  pack guard fails the PR on a content edit without it. This is separate from the
  project version and is **not** automated.

The invariant is NOT "main == last tag" — it is **"a tag's version tells the
truth about shipped content"**: two tags with different versions always differ
in what users actually run. Mechanically:

- A merge **requires a version bump** when its diff touches the **shipped

- The bump **rides the shipped-surface PR itself** — do not open a separate
  `chore(release)` bump PR; merging the bumped PR IS cutting the release
  (§5). When several shipped PRs deliberately accumulate before a release,
  the final PR of the batch carries the bump.
- Merges touching only CI workflows, docs, tests, or repo tooling do **not**
  bump. Main being ahead of the last tag by that class of change is not
  drift — it's the definition.
- Never cut a release tag while unversioned shipped-surface changes sit on
  `main`; bump first.

Rationale: upgrades are not free for users (multi-GB container pull, upgrade
paths with real failure modes), and the release-check nudges every install.
Don't spend that on housekeeping — release when shipped value has accumulated.
The test for "internal change" is just: *does the wheel or image change?* —
answerable from the diff paths. (v6.1.1 predates this rule: it shipped a
byte-identical wheel for CI-only changes; harmless, but the nudge was wasted.)

When you bump the version you MUST also:

- **Regenerate and commit `uv.lock`** in the same change — the lock pins
  `agentalloy`'s own version, so a `pyproject`-only bump leaves them drifted. CI
  uses `uv sync --frozen` (uses the lock as-is) and will **not** catch the drift;
  it only bites a `uv sync --locked` run or a merge. Verify with `uv lock --check`
  (output `Resolved N packages` = clean).

- **Bump the touched pack's `version`** if you edited any `src/agentalloy/_packs/<pack>/`
  content (e.g. `pack.yaml`). Pack propagation is version-gated by design (preserves
  the SkillVersion rollback chain), and a CI guard fails the PR on a content edit
  without a version bump.

Four required checks on `main`: **`quality`**, **`container-tests`**,

- `pipx-smoke`: builds the core wheel, installs it isolated, smoke-tests the

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Derive the automatic SemVer bump for a PR from its Conventional-Commit title.

The version BUMP is no longer a human decision (RELEASE.md §4): CI runs this to
compute the next version and writes ``pyproject.toml`` + ``uv.lock`` on the PR
branch. Two gates, both deterministic:

- *Whether* to bump: the diff must touch the **shipped surface** (``src/``,
  ``frontend/``, container, dep pins) — docs/CI/test-only PRs don't version.
- *Which tier*: read from the PR title — ``feat!``/``BREAKING CHANGE`` → major,
  ``feat`` → minor, everything else touching shipped code → patch. The
  "else → patch" default honours §4's invariant (*a tag's version tells the
  truth about shipped content*) with zero human judgement.

The pure functions below carry no I/O and are unit-tested in
``tests/test_version_bump.py`` (mirrors the ``test_pack_version_bump_guard.py``
ethos). ``main`` does the git reads and prints the next version to stdout, or
nothing when no bump is warranted (docs-only, or the PR is already bumped —
idempotent, so the job's own push re-runs to a clean no-op).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Literal

Tier = Literal["major", "minor", "patch"]

# Shipped surface — a change here means users run different bytes, so it must
# version (RELEASE.md §4). Single source of truth; keep in lockstep with the
# doc and with test_pack_version_bump_guard's _PACKS_PREFIX (a subset here).
SHIPPED_DIR_PREFIXES = ("src/", "frontend/", "container/")
SHIPPED_EXACT_FILES = ("pyproject.toml", "uv.lock")  # dependency pins
SHIPPED_FILE_PREFIXES = ("Containerfile",)  # Containerfile, Containerfile.dev, …

# type(scope)!: subject  —  scope and the breaking "!" are both optional.
_CONVENTIONAL = re.compile(r"^\s*(?P<type>[a-zA-Z]+)(?:\([^)]*\))?(?P<bang>!)?:")


def tier_from_title(title: str) -> Tier:
    """Map a Conventional-Commit PR title to a SemVer tier.

    ``feat!`` / a ``BREAKING CHANGE`` marker → major; ``feat`` → minor;
    anything else (``fix``, ``perf``, ``refactor``, ``chore``, or a title that
    doesn't parse) → patch. Never returns None: the no-bump decision belongs to
    :func:`touches_shipped_surface`, not to the tier.
    """
    if "BREAKING CHANGE" in title or "BREAKING-CHANGE" in title:
        return "major"
    m = _CONVENTIONAL.match(title)
    if m is None:
        return "patch"
    if m.group("bang"):
        return "major"
    if m.group("type").lower() == "feat":
        return "minor"
    return "patch"


def touches_shipped_surface(changed_files: list[str]) -> bool:
    """True if any changed path is part of the shipped wheel/image surface."""
    for f in changed_files:
        p = f.strip()
        if not p:
            continue
        if p in SHIPPED_EXACT_FILES:
            return True
        if p.startswith(SHIPPED_DIR_PREFIXES):
            return True
        if p.startswith(SHIPPED_FILE_PREFIXES):
            return True
    return False


def bump(version: str, tier: Tier) -> str:
    """Return ``version`` advanced by ``tier``, resetting lower components."""
    parts = version.split(".")
    if len(parts) != 3 or not all(part.isdigit() for part in parts):
        raise ValueError(f"not a plain X.Y.Z version: {version!r}")
    major, minor, patch = (int(part) for part in parts)
    if tier == "major":
        return f"{major + 1}.0.0"
    if tier == "minor":
        return f"{major}.{minor + 1}.0"
    return f"{major}.{minor}.{patch + 1}"


def decide(title: str, changed_files: list[str], current_version: str) -> str | None:
    """Compute the next version for a PR, or None when no bump is warranted."""
    if not touches_shipped_surface(changed_files):
        return None
    return bump(current_version, tier_from_title(title))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# I/O boundary — git reads + pyproject parse; kept out of the pure logic above
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

_VERSION_LINE = re.compile(r'^version = "(?P<v>[^"]+)"', re.MULTILINE)


def _version_from_pyproject_text(text: str) -> str | None:
    m = _VERSION_LINE.search(text)
    return m.group("v") if m else None


def _read_current_version(pyproject: Path) -> str | None:
    return _version_from_pyproject_text(pyproject.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


def _git(args: list[str], repo_root: Path) -> str:
    return subprocess.run(
        ["git", *args],
        cwd=repo_root,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=True,
    ).stdout


def _version_at_ref(base_sha: str, repo_root: Path) -> str | None:
    try:
        text = _git(["show", f"{base_sha}:pyproject.toml"], repo_root)
    except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
        return None
    return _version_from_pyproject_text(text)


def _changed_files(base_sha: str, repo_root: Path) -> list[str]:
    # Two-dot diff (base vs working HEAD), matching test_pack_version_bump_guard.
    out = _git(["diff", "--name-only", base_sha], repo_root)
    return [line for line in out.splitlines() if line.strip()]


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--title", required=True, help="PR title (conventional commit)")
    parser.add_argument("--base-sha", required=True, help="PR base commit SHA")
    parser.add_argument("--repo-root", default=".", help="repo root (default: cwd)")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    repo_root = Path(args.repo_root).resolve()
    pyproject = repo_root / "pyproject.toml"

    current = _read_current_version(pyproject)
    if current is None:
        print("error: no version in pyproject.toml", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    # Idempotency: if the branch already carries a bump (version differs from
    # base), emit nothing so the job's own re-triggered run is a clean no-op.
    base_version = _version_at_ref(args.base_sha, repo_root)
    if base_version is not None and base_version != current:
        return 0

    changed = _changed_files(args.base_sha, repo_root)
    nxt = decide(args.title, changed, current)
    if nxt is not None:
        print(nxt)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

# job's own push re-triggered the run), the script emits nothing and the job is
# a clean green no-op. release-cut.yml is untouched — it still cuts the tag when
# the untagged version lands on main and CI is green.

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, edited]

concurrency:
  group: version-bump-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read # the bump commit is pushed with BUMP_TOKEN, not GITHUB_TOKEN

jobs:
  version-bump:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Check out PR head branch
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          # head_ref = the PR's source branch (not the detached merge ref), so
          # we can commit + push back to it. fetch-depth 0: the script reads the
          # base commit's pyproject and the base..HEAD diff.
          ref: ${{ github.head_ref }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          token: ${{ secrets.BUMP_TOKEN }}

      - name: Install uv
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v3
        with:
          enable-cache: true

      - name: Compute and apply version bump
        env:
          PR_TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          next=$(uv run python scripts/version_bump.py \
            --title "$PR_TITLE" --base-sha "$BASE_SHA")

          if [ -z "$next" ]; then
            echo "No version bump warranted (no shipped-surface change, or already bumped)."
            exit 0
          fi

          echo "Deriving bump → v$next"
          # Exactly one top-level `version = "..."` line in pyproject.toml.
          sed -i -E "s/^version = \"[^\"]+\"/version = \"$next\"/" pyproject.toml
          uv lock

          git config user.name "agentalloy-release-bot"
          git config user.email "release-bot@users.noreply.github.com"
          git add pyproject.toml uv.lock
          git commit -m "chore: bump version to $next" \
            -m "Automated bump derived from the PR title's Conventional-Commit type." \
            -m "Co-Authored-By: agentalloy-release-bot <release-bot@users.noreply.github.com>"
          git push origin "HEAD:${{ github.head_ref }}"
